required_outcomes: Replies to the landlord with an accurate update: the tenant swapped in their own machine on 24 December, his faulty machine is stored in the garage, no contractor has been sent, and the request was closed without his being told, with an apology for that.
Asks the landlord what he wants done with his machine (inspect and repair, or dispose) and whether the tenant's machine may stay connected.

Recognises that the tenant was told on 24 December that someone would check the machine when they are back, and either reopens the request or sets a dated follow-up to settle that once the landlord answers.
acceptable_alternatives: Phoning the landlord rather than emailing, provided the call is logged and covers the same points.
Leaving the request closed and recording the landlord's answer as a follow-up, provided the tenant's expectation of a visit is dealt with when the landlord replies.
positive_behaviours: Adds a note to the record that the case was closed without the landlord being informed, so the gap is visible.
Avoids proposing any visit while the tenants are on holiday.
Records that the machine in use belongs to the tenant.
red_flags: Telling the landlord a visit is arranged or that someone will check the machine, when nothing has been booked.
Escalating a routine landlord update to a human.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a contractor or booking a visit before the landlord has said what he wants.
Inventing a date for the check the tenant was promised.
critical_failures: Leaving the landlord's question unanswered, or telling him nothing is needed without explaining that the tenant has replaced his machine.
